meta.title: 79 Beach Bar & Restaurant · A growth audit for Don
meta.description: A complimentary growth audit for Don, owner of 79 Beach Bar & Restaurant on Klong Muang Beach, Krabi. Prepared by Dan at Green Isle Marketing.

commercial.badge: Free audit · a referral is the thank-you

video.title: Hi Don.
video.welcome: Hi Don — Dan here, from Green Isle Marketing in Krabi. This audit is free. Press play and I’ll walk you through it.

snapshot.title: A loved beach bar.
snapshot.lead: Public listings checked on 31 October 2026. Nothing on Google, Tripadvisor or Facebook has been changed. Counts move, and a manager login would confirm anything the public page hides.
snapshot.scoreNote: Strong product. Weak packaging. 58 is an audit score, not a Google ranking.
snapshot.issuesTitle: What is getting in the way

issues.title: Two different phone numbers
issues.detail: Google shows +66 65 961 6141. Tripadvisor shows +66 63 254 5337. Guests cannot tell which one reaches the floor.

issues.title: No owned website or booking page
issues.detail: There is no restaurant website. A table request has nowhere clear to land, and Google is effectively offering an empty website field.

issues.title: A thin Facebook page
issues.detail: About 248 followers. The bio reads “Come and join us for at our beach front bar…” and the location label says Ban Ao Nang. 79 is on Klong Muang Beach, not Ao Nang centre.

issues.title: Thin name, address and phone details
issues.detail: Google’s public address is essentially “83, 81000”. Guests search Klong Muang Beach and Nong Thale. The same facts should match on every listing.

issues.title: Tripadvisor is underweight
issues.detail: 4.5 from 54 reviews, beside 595 on Google. Happy tables are not being asked, equally, to leave a Tripadvisor review.

snapshot.aside: This is not Bar 79 & Grill on Pruksa Uthit Road in Krabi Town. Different business, different listing. The page name should always sit next to Klong Muang Beach.

posts.text:
Hi from 79 on Klong Muang Beach.

Thai food, cold drinks, sunset in the sand, live DJ and fire shows at night.

Planning dinner or a group? Message us or WhatsApp for a table — or use the link for directions and reviews.

About 15 minutes from Ao Nang. See you by the sea.
The light goes gold, then the lamps come on. Message us if you want a table tonight.
Seafood, Pad Thai, Tom Kha, something to share. Ask what the kitchen is cooking today — photos should match the plate.
A slower lunch, feet almost in the sand. Families and travellers, both welcome.

posts.text: Klong Muang Beach. Quieter than Ao Nang, about 15 minutes away. This is not Bar 79 in Krabi Town.
DJ, fire show, happy hour — ask what is actually on tonight. We will not post a time we have not confirmed.

before.title: What guests see today
before.lead: About 248 followers. The bio is one thin line. The location label says Ban Ao Nang. Posting is quiet. Checked in public on 31 October 2026.
bullets: Location label points at Ban Ao Nang. 79 sits on Klong Muang Beach.
The bio reads “Come and join us for at our beach front bar…” and does not name Klong Muang Beach.
About 248 followers, and the page does not show a steady run of sunset, food and night posts.
Hours, one phone number and a clear request for a table are easy to miss.
The live page is still at facebook.com/79Beachbarandrestaurant. Nothing on it has been changed.

changes.change: Put Klong Muang Beach in the name line, bio and cover
changes.why: Facebook matches pages to what people type and where they are — naming the real beach helps your page show up for “beach bar Klong Muang”.

changes.change: Fix the location away from Ban Ao Nang
changes.why: Wrong town sends locals and hotel guests to the wrong map pin, so your page looks irrelevant when they search nearby.

changes.change: Add WhatsApp + Message as the main buttons
changes.why: A one-tap ask for a table turns browsers into booked seats instead of silent scrollers.

changes.change: Complete hours, category and “good to know”
changes.why: Full details help Facebook recommend you in search and keep guests from bouncing to a clearer competitor page.

changes.change: Pin a welcome post and keep 3–4 fresh posts (sunset, food, nights)
changes.why: Recent posts and photos signal an open, lively bar — quiet pages get skipped in recommendations.

changes.change: Show real review quotes and reply in public
changes.why: Reviews and owner replies build trust in the feed and in Facebook’s recommendations, without buying stars.

changes.change: Use the same name, phone and address as Google
changes.why: Matching details across Facebook and Maps stop guests from wondering if they found the right 79.

fixes.title: One phone number everywhere
fixes.detail: Pick the number that actually rings on the floor. Put that same number on Google, Tripadvisor, Facebook, WhatsApp and the website. Retire the other one in public, or say clearly what each line is for.
fixes.why: Maps ranks clearer, trusted listings higher — one ringing number stops lost calls and mixed signals.

fixes.title: Write the address the way guests search
fixes.detail: Replace the thin “83, 81000” line with Klong Muang Beach, Nong Thale, Krabi 81180. Confirm the exact approach and pin with Don before anyone moves it.
fixes.why: Relevance and distance both matter: if the address says the beach guests type, you show up when they are nearby.

fixes.title: Add the website, then a real request link
fixes.detail: When you approve the page, put it in the website field. Link the booking action to the request form or WhatsApp. Do not promise instant confirmation.
fixes.why: A website and action button make the profile look complete, which helps prominence and turns map views into table asks.

fixes.when: The next two to four weeks
fixes.title: Categories, attributes, photos, posts
fixes.detail: Keep Restaurant and Bar. Tick beachfront, outdoor seating and live music only where they are true and Google offers the field. Upload a tight owner set: sunset, tree at night, four dishes, entrance, families. Post twice a week in high season, in English and Thai, only about things that are actually on.
fixes.why: Primary/secondary categories, beachfront attributes, and fresh photos tell Google what you are and that you are active.

fixes.when: The next two to four weeks
fixes.title: Answer the questions people already ask
fixes.detail: Do you take bookings? Is there parking? How far from Ao Nang? Are children welcome? Do you take cards? Tripadvisor currently says cash. If that is wrong, correct it. If it is right, say so.
fixes.why: Answered questions keep guests on your listing instead of hunting another bar that already spelled it out.

fixes.title: Replies, and menu photos that match the plate
fixes.detail: Thank a 5-star review within a couple of days, and mention the night, not a template. For a 3-star or below, apologise, invite a private message, and do not argue a portion in public. Fix the photo instead. Recent Tripadvisor notes mention waits, spice and dishes that did not match the picture.
fixes.why: Fast, human replies and honest photos lift trust — review volume and response rate both feed prominence over time.

reviewPlan.title: Review growth, without the tricks
reviewPlan.lead: More new reviews from real tables, on Google and Tripadvisor, through high season. A direction, not a promise.

rows.tactic: QR on the table and the bill
rows.how: Two codes, Google and Tripadvisor, for every table. “Takes about half a minute.”

rows.tactic: A morning note, only if they shared a number
rows.how: Optional WhatsApp or LINE the next day. Same ask, happy or not.

rows.tactic: A soft ask from the floor
rows.how: After dessert or a second round, when the table is at ease. Never only the smiling tables.
Honest dish photos, a spice check, a word about tide and weather for sand-side seats.
Future guests can see a person is there.

reviewPlan.never: Never buy reviews, never hand the QR only to happy tables, and never offer a free drink for a star rating. That breaks Google and Tripadvisor rules, and it is not how 79 got to 4.7.
kpis: Share of reviews replied to within 48 hours
Direction requests and calls, once Don opens the insights

google.pairNote: Both cards are Green Isle mockups, not a Google screen. The first uses the public listing from the 31 October 2026 audit. The second is the same profile with the beach named, one phone, a website and owner photos. The 4.7 from 595 reviews is the real public figure. Nothing has been published.

plan.title: Tourists in season.
plan.titleEm: Locals the rest of the week.
plan.lead: The positioning, in one line: the easy sunset table on Klong Muang Beach. Thai food, a real welcome, DJ and fire-show nights, about 15 minutes from Ao Nang.
plan.disclaimer: Results are not guaranteed. Covers, rankings and revenue depend on the food, the service, how many seats you have, the season, the weather, any ad spend, and how fast the phone number and photos get fixed. This plan does not promise a number-one map pin, a sell-out, or a return on ads.

items.title: Hotels and concierges
items.body: A one-page card: pin, hours, a few dishes, and “mention the hotel”. Klong Muang, Tubkaak and nearby resorts, plus Ao Nang desks that send people west. A tasting for staff once. Commission only if you want it — many partners just need their guests looked after.

items.title: Google
items.body: Fix the phone, address, photos and posts first. Then the website field and the table request. A small geo test around Klong Muang and Ao Nang is optional, on phrases like “Klong Muang restaurant” and “sunset dinner Krabi”. Pause it if the cost per enquiry is weak.

items.title: Meta, geo-targeted
items.body: Real sunset, a fire-show clip, a Thai plate, a family table. Radius around Ao Nang, Klong Muang and Railay overnights. Late-afternoon ads, when people are choosing dinner. Land on the request form or WhatsApp.

items.title: Tripadvisor
items.body: The listing is claimed. Reply to every review. Grow from 54 with the same honest QR you use for Google. Sponsored placement only after the photos and replies are in good shape.

items.title: Weekly nights, agreed with you
items.body: Ideas, not a published calendar: a midweek locals set, an earlier family Sunday, one night worth posting. We put them on the page only after you pick the evening and the offer.

items.title: LINE and the community
items.body: A LINE Official Account, or a simple broadcast list to start: today’s menu, tonight’s show time, a last-minute table. Useful posts in local groups, not spam.

items.title: The people already nearby
items.body: Klong Muang residents and long-stay rentals do not need a tourist funnel. They need a reason to come on a Tuesday and a message that reaches them.

timeline.name: Foundation
points: Lock one phone, WhatsApp and LINE.
Clean Google and Tripadvisor details, photos and the short description in English and Thai.
Refresh Facebook: bio, cover, pin, two-week calendar.
Table QR for Google and Tripadvisor.
List ten hotel and concierge targets. Speak to the first five.

timeline.name: Demand
points: A small Meta geo test, two creatives.
A concierge tasting or a flyer drop.
Reply to reviews and post on Google every week.

timeline.name: Refine
points: Keep what brings tables. Stop what does not.
Push group and event requests around the travel peaks you actually want.
Sit down on the numbers and decide whether you want a paid retainer or to run it yourselves.
If you are happy, introductions to two or three other owners.

kpis.name: Partner hotels actually sending guests
kpis.where: A simple list, plus a mention at the table

plan.budget: Ads are optional and yours to approve. A sensible first test is about 3,000–8,000 baht a month, not a quote. Domain, LINE and a half-day of photos are small and separate. Nothing here has been switched on.

pricing.title: A clear fee.
pricing.intro: For paid proposals. This 79 audit does not use this section.

close.title: This audit is free.
close.titleEm: If it helps, pass my name on.
paragraphs: Don, there is no fee for this audit, the page concept, the Facebook redesign or the 90-day plan. I am not asking you to buy a retainer on the back of a sunset.
You already did the hard part. The beach, the food and 595 Google reviews are yours. I would like to help more of the right people find the place.
If you are happy with the work, I would be grateful for a recommendation, or an introduction to another bar or restaurant owner. There is no obligation, and no awkward script. A forward is enough.
close.ask: Two or three introductions, when it feels right. Hotels, tours and other kitchens all count.
close.forwardable: I’ve been looking at how people find 79 Beach Bar with Dan at Green Isle Marketing in Krabi. If you own a bar or restaurant and want a straight look at your Google, Facebook and website, he’s worth a conversation: dan@greenislemarketing.com
close.whatsappText: Hi Dan, it's Don from 79 Beach Bar. I had a look at the audit.
